explanation.question_quote: Cardiac exam reveals a systolic murmur best heard at the lower left sternal border that radiates to the axilla.
explanation.sentence: This 20-year-old athlete has recurrent exertional syncope and a systolic murmur best heard at the lower left sternal border.
Recurrent exertional syncope with a systolic murmur in a young athlete suggests hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy.
Squatting increases preload and afterload, reducing dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction and making the murmur softer.
Mitral stenosis produces a diastolic rumble, whereas aortic stenosis is typically loudest at the right upper sternal border and radiates to the carotids.
